newsitem.title: UK: Unilever lifts first quarter profits 7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Unilever lifts first quarter profits 7 pct.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch foods and consumer products group Unilever NV/Plc reported a seven percent increase in first-quarter profits to 538 million pounds on Friday, in a low key statement reflecting a weak trading environment.

The company said sales in Europe were slightly ahead and profits rose sharply, but profits in North America fell by 11 percent as foods and prestige businesses made a slow start to the year after a strong end to 1996.
In the Asia-Pacific region, sales advanced and profits were much higher but in Latin America, trading profits were affected by increased marketing investment and higher costs in Brazil.

Europe was the group's star performer with trading profits before exceptional items leaping to 360 million from 254 million pounds ($412.2 million), driven by sales of foods and personal care products.
"Benefits from restructuring and portfolio management contibuted to the profit improvement, which was further boosted by a different phasing of central costs," the group said.
The contribution to group profits, however, from Africa and the Middle East almost halved to 17 million pounds due to a decline in sales after a major shake-up of distribution in Turkey.

At constant rates of exchange sales increased by five perecent to 7.988 billion pounds. At current rates of exchange, net profit fell eight percent in sterling to 296 million, reflecting the relative strength of the British currency, but increased by 11 percent in Dutch guilders.

Trading profit before exceptional items rose 16 percent to 661 million pounds. Total exceptionals for the quarter rose to 76 million from 15 million, mainly due to restructuring in foods businesses in Europe including the charge for a head office in Bristol.
Net debt was 1.905 billion pounds at the end of the quarter down almost 900 million pounds due to a much better cashflow from the group's operations. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
